newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

IMF and World Bank representatives in Colombo say economic performance in 1996 is "praiseworthy and satisfactory", in light of shocks like ballooning defence spending and crippling drought. Deputy Minister of Finance G. L. Peiris told parliament last week that GDP growth for 1996 should be about 3.7 percent.

Over 6,000 Tamils, including public servants and university students have returned to northern Jaffna peninsula from Vavunia in northest, despite claims to the contrary by LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eealam) and some NGOs', officials say.
Six policemen and four homeguards and five rebels die in clash in Arlaganvila, in north central Sri Lanka.

Criminal investigation department (CID) questions two senior police officers regarding allegations of a torture chamber at a state housing completx at Batalanda, a Colombo suburb. Opposition leader Ranil Wickremesinghe was also questioned last week.

Scotland Yard arrests a Sri Lankan who allegedly made bogus phone calls about a tiger suicide squad that had moved into the vicinity of President Kumaratunga's official residence, Temple Trees, on October 8. The search operation that followed led to the biggest traffic jam Colombo has seen in recent times.
Police warn public to be extra vigilant in the next few days, as LTTE leader Prabakaran's birthday and the organisation's "Martyr's Week" falls later in November.
